messages:
Ethan S: FYI - Ion yx team (Alex) wants to run a POC with a new model they trained called ionyx-65b. Asking if we can onboard it into the catalog quickly and provide cost/latency estimates. They also sent a security questionnaire.
Rina K: thanks Ethan. quick q: is ionyx-65b a LLaMA-derivative or more custom (custom ops)? any exported artifacts (hf .pt / ggml)?
Ethan S: Alex said they have both a HuggingFace repo + a Torch state_dict. no docker. they mentioned a fused rmsnorm in the arch but not 100% sure.
Priya G: big flag if it's using a custom fused RMSNorm kernel. our runtime can fallback to a non-fused path but that often doubles per-token latency for 65B at 4k seq. need these checks:
- confirm model dtype + tokenizer (bpe/spm)
- fasta run of shape and kv cache layout
- a quick forward trace to detect unsupported ops
Rina K: can you run a compatibility scan, Priya? customer wants to start hosted POC but may want Dedicated if latency/cost look bad.
Priya G: yes I can run a scan. ask Alex for:
- a small model tarball (first 2 layers) or the HF repo link
- example prompts and target seq len (p50/p95)
Also, send the model config so I can run `redwood-compat-check` locally.
Priya G: snippet to run once we have the HF repo:
```
# clone & quick-compat
git clone https://hf.co/example/ionyx-65b && cd ionyx-65b
python -m redwood.tools.compat_check --model-dir . --output report.json
```
Priya G: compat_check will flag ops not in our kernel registry and estimate a performance delta.
Ben M: security side - Alex, two quick asks: 1) will any customer PII be part of prompts? 2) do you require Redwood hosted or a Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment for the POC? we need that for the questionnaire.
Alex R: no PII in prompts for the POC, just product descriptions & internal docs. We prefer Hosted to move faster, but if SLA/attestation is required we might need Dedicated.
Ethan S: Alex also asked for a rough cost estimate: target ~100k tokens/day, target p50 latency ~150ms, p95 <500ms. any back-of-envelope numbers?
Priya G: ballpark: running 65B on hosted with our standard quantized path (4-bit) we expect ~0.9-1.2M tokens per GPU per day depending on batching. Pricing estimate for 100k tokens/day on hosted: approx $800-1200/month (token + infra amortized) — very rough until we know batch profile. latency depends on fallback: if fused ops supported -> p50 ~120-160ms, if fallback -> p50 could be 250-350ms.
Rina K: OK — recommend two paths for the POC:
1) Hosted fast-track: run compat scan, onboard as a transient catalog variant (quant4) and run evals. Shortest time-to-demo.
2) Dedicated trial: reserved capacity if they need stricter p95 + contractual SLA.
Alex R: we can start with Hosted. I'll upload the HF repo link and a filled security questionnaire today.
DeployBot: :package: uploaded artifact ionyx-65b-repo.tar.gz (size: 1.1GB) by Alex R at 1729502800
Priya G: got the repo. started compat check now. first pass shows 'fused_rmsnorm' and 'attention_rotary_fused' ops not in kernel registry. generating report.
Priya G: report summary: 1) fused_rmsnorm -> fallback (2.1x token latency hit) 2) rotary fused op -> fallback (1.3x) 3) tokenizer uses bpe - compatible
Priya G: recommendation: we can ship a POC hosted variant if customer accepts higher latency or we provide a quantized variant with custom conversion to replace fused ops (takes ~3-5 days devtime). Alternatively, customer can provide a converted checkpoint.
Ben M: from security - Hosted is fine for this POC given no PII, but we need SOC2 cert and terms acknowedged. Alex, please confirm you accept our data processing addendum and we'll share SOC2 report.
Alex R: confirm, we'll sign the DPA and want the SOC2 report before starting real traffic.
Ethan S: next steps: (1) Alex upload converted checkpoint or accept 3-5 day kernel conversion; (2) Priya finish compat report + perf estimate; (3) Ben share SOC2 + DPA; (4) Rina prepare Hosted POC pricing quote. aiming to demo in 1 week.
Rina K: I'll draft a hosted POC quote and include contingency pricing for Dedicated if perf regressions unacceptable.
Priya G: finishing perf numbers now, will post report.json and small perf table shortly.
Priya G: report posted: https://redwood.internal/reports/1729502468-ionyx-compat (internal)
Priya G: perf table (p50/p95 estimates): fused kernels present -> p50 140ms / p95 420ms; with fallback -> p50 320ms / p95 820ms; with conversion -> p50 150ms / p95 460ms
Ethan S: perfect. Alex, do you want us to proceed with Hosted fast-track assuming conversion delay or do you want to send converted checkpoint?
Alex R: we want to proceed asap. go ahead with Hosted fast-track and start with quant4 variant. we'll plan for conversion later if needed.
Rina K: noted, I'll send the quote and PO template by EOD.
Ben M: I'll DM Alex for DPA signature flow and share SOC2 link.
Ethan S: thanks everyone — updating the deal in Hub and scheduling a follow-up demo next Tues.
